text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Expelled United National Independence Party (UNIP) central committee member Sam Moyo has charged several party members, including vice-president Inyambo Yeta, of plotting to remove Kenneth Kaunda as party leader.
- Sweden says Zambia has made progress in fostering good governance, and recommended against a proposed media council bill, which it said would undermine this.
- Over 50 Zairean government officials and their families fled into Zambia at the weekend after angry villagers turned on them.
- Finance and Economic Development Minister Ronald Penza says Zambia's financial system is a positive force for economic growth and development.
